Complete the summary below.

Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.
groups.content:
Longships and knarrs

The hull of a Viking ship was made of overlapping planks, which were attached to each other with iron [6]. The planks were split from the trunks of [7] trees rather than being sawn. To make the hull watertight, the gaps were filled with animal hair that had been soaked in [8].

Longships had a shallow hull, so they could be dragged up onto [9]. Their single square sail was made of [10], and the rowers probably sat on [11] which held their possessions.

Knarrs were broader and deeper than longships and depended mostly on their [12]. As well as animals and timber, they carried goods such as walrus [13].

Cropmarks appear because crops above buried features are affected differently by dry weather. The soft soil in an old ditch holds more [20], so the crops above it remain green. Over buried walls, the soil is thin, and the crops become [21] earlier. In 2018, as well as photographs taken from an aircraft, the survey team received pictures taken by the public using [22].

Questions 38-40

Complete the sentences below.

Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage for each answer.
groups.content:
38. Most of a plant's cells only change state after it has experienced several weeks of [38].

39. Because of warmer winters, some fruit growers have seen uneven flowering and reduced [39].

40. The research was done using a plant called [40], which is related to cabbage.

questions.explanation: Answer: FALSE Viking ships were built by eye, ' without any written plans at all '.
Answer: NOT GIVEN We learn when and why the Oseberg ship was buried, but not its size or how it compares with other ships.
Answer: FALSE Ships were built 'from the outside in': ' Only once the shell of the hull was complete were the internal ribs added '.
Answer: TRUE The shallow hull let them be dragged onto beaches, ' so that their crews could land almost anywhere without the need for a harbour '.
Answer: TRUE ' The rowers were not slaves but the warriors themselves '.
Answer: rivets 'each plank was fixed to the one below it with iron rivets '.
Answer: oak 'The planks were usually split from trunks of oak rather than sawn'.
Answer: tar 'filled with animal hair soaked in tar to keep the water out'.
Answer: beaches The shallow hull allowed longships 'to be dragged up onto beaches '.
Answer: wool 'a single large square sail made of wool '.
Answer: chests With no fixed benches, rowers 'are thought to have sat on wooden chests containing their personal belongings'.
Answer: sail Knarrs 'relied mainly on their sail , carrying only a few oars'.
Answer: ivory 'A knarr could carry livestock, timber, wool and walrus ivory '.
Answer: B Rain or harvest can make cropmarks disappear, so ' archaeologists have to record them as fast as they can before the opportunity is lost '.
Answer: G The Roman estates produced grain and ' also sold wool, leather and cattle '.
Answer: D The ditch and bank ' would have served to keep farm animals in and wild animals out '.
Answer: F On clay soils, life was hard 'in wet years, when the soil stayed flooded and crops could easily fail '.
Answer: C 'It was exhausting' – early starts and ' hours circling in a hot, cramped cockpit '.
Answer: H More frequent dry summers ' could reveal many more sites in the years ahead '.
Answer: moisture Over a filled ditch, 'the ground holds more moisture , so the crops above it stay green for longer'.
Answer: yellow Over walls the soil dries quickly and 'the crops there turn yellow first'.
Answer: drones Members of the public took part, 'using drones to photograph fields near their homes'.

text.en: Most of the sites were burial monuments.
Some sites were on land that was thought to have been avoided by farmers.
People who were not archaeologists contributed to the survey.
Drone photographs proved more useful than those taken from the aircraft.
More new sites were found in Wales than in England.

questions.explanation: Answer: B, C Farmers were assumed to avoid clay, ' Yet a large number of the newly discovered farmsteads lay on exactly this kind of ground ' (B); 'Members of the public also took part' (C). Many sites were farmsteads, not burial mounds (A); no comparison is made for D or E.

text.en: They helped to supply soldiers with food.
They were owned by army officers.
They were connected to places where goods could be sold.
They sent most of their produce overseas.
They were larger than modern farms in the same area.

questions.explanation: Answer: A, C They ' produced grain for the army ' (A), and ' roads and tracks show how the estates were linked to nearby markets ' (C). Nothing is said about ownership (B), exports (D) or modern farms (E).
Answer: NOT GIVEN We are told which institute the team is from, but nothing about the nationalities of its members.
Answer: TRUE ' This prevents them from flowering during a mild spell in autumn ', which would expose the flowers to winter.
Answer: FALSE ' His claims were later shown to be false '.
Answer: TRUE ' Each cell makes its own decision, flipping from on to off '.
Answer: FALSE Once switched off, FLC ' stays off even when the weather warms up again ', so the plant remembers the winter for weeks or months.
Answer: NOT GIVEN Both apples and cherries need chilling, but the passage does not compare how much each has been affected.
Answer: G 'If we understand exactly how plants measure the cold, we may be able to breed varieties that need less of it '.
Answer: A ' The research, published this month in a leading scientific journal '.
Answer: H ' the team is now working with plant breeders who will test whether the findings can be applied to these crops '.
Answer: B Flowering in a mild autumn spell ' would expose their delicate flowers and seeds to the harsh winter that follows '.
Answer: C Farmers decide when to sow: ' Winter varieties of wheat and barley are sown in autumn so that they experience the cold they need '.
Answer: cold 'a plant typically needs several weeks of cold before most of its cells have changed state'.
Answer: yields 'growers have reported uneven flowering and lower yields '.
Answer: thale cress 'The work was carried out on thale cress , a small plant related to cabbage'.
